subject: Hosted API: p99 latency spike affecting Satori Health - incident & comms
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@satorihealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: sre@satorihealth.com, ops@satorihealth.com
Date: 2026-08-30T18:12:00Z
Subject: Severe p99 latency spikes in Hosted API impacting inference throughput

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing intermittent p99 latency spikes in calls to your hosted API since ~17:40 UTC. At peak we’re observing 2-3x increases in p99 and throughput drops (~40% request success rate for short bursts). This is affecting our live triage pipeline and causing timeouts in our downstream workers.

Metrics we captured (short window):
- 2026-08-30 17:41–17:52 UTC: p95 ~420ms (normal ~120ms), p99 ~2.4s (normal ~450ms)
- Error rate from client side: 6.8% during spikes
- Concurrent QPS for our key endpoint: 120 -> backing off after errors

We raised this with our SRE but need Redwood to confirm whether this is internal (routing/serving) vs model degradation. Please advise immediate mitigation — even a temporary fallback to a lower-latency model would help.

This is blocking our weekend release. Can you escalate?

Thanks,
Emma Liu
Lead Infrastructure Engineer
Satori Health

Subject: RE: Severe p99 latency spikes in Hosted API impacting inference throughput

Quick summary from infra: we see elevated tail latency correlated with a spike in long-sequence requests hitting the 2nd-stage KV cache miss path. Root causes under investigation — early hypothesis: cache eviction churn after a nightly indexing job plus a deployment of a new kernel selection heuristic.

Immediate mitigations attempted (18:35–18:40 UTC):
- Enabled aggressive prefix/KV warming for affected model pool (partial improvement for some customers).
- Rolled back kernel heuristic in a canary subset (candidate rollback showed p99 drop ~40% for that subset).
- Suggest routing Satori to the canary/backoff variant (lower latency, slightly higher token cost) until we finish a full rollback and cache warm.

Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (generated from serving logs) — contains per-region p95/p99 and error-rate samples.

Next steps: full rollback of kernel heuristic across APAC and aggressive cache re-warm; will update in 20–30m with metrics.

-Markus
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks for flagging this. We’ve opened an incident and our engineers have identified a likely regression in a kernel-selection heuristic that increased KV cache churn. Mitigations are active:
- Canary rollback in APAC is underway (shows initial improvement)
- Aggressive cache re-warm for affected model pools
- Temporary traffic routing to a lower-latency model variant if you want immediate stability (expect slightly higher token cost)

Subject: Post-incident follow-up & next steps (Hosted API latency, 2026-08-30)

Emma / Satori team —

Thanks again for your patience while we resolved the APAC tail latency incident from 2026-08-30. Summary and next steps:

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-08-30 17:40–19:05 UTC (mitigations began ~18:35 UTC).
- Impact: elevated p99 latency and transient error rates for a subset of APAC traffic.
- Root cause: regression in kernel-selection heuristic leading to KV cache eviction churn during a nightly indexing job.
- Immediate fix: full rollback of the heuristic in APAC and aggressive cache re-warm; optional traffic routing to fallback model for immediate stability.

What we’ve delivered:
- Incident timeline and per-region metrics attached (incident-timeline.csv).
- Public incident entry posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260830-9
- JIRA for engineering follow-up: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4579
- Postmortem draft and action-item tracker: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/INC-2026-08-30+Latency+Postmortem

Action owners / next steps:
- Markus: complete regression test and sign off on heuristic rework (ETA 2026-09-07).
- Engineering: add guardrails to prevent cache-churn-prone heuristic from shipping without region canary (owner: Markus).
- Evelyn/Rishi: coordinate a short executive summary for your stakeholders (ETA 2026-09-03).
- Dylan: finalize incident timeline and ensure alerting thresholds adjusted to detect early KV churn patterns (ETA 2026-09-02).

If you’d like a short call with our eng/ops leads to walk through the timeline and planned mitigations, I can schedule one this week.

Appreciate your partnership — we’ll share the finalized postmortem and will follow up with any compensatory credits if applicable per contract (DEAL-8251).
